candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — financial barriers to cancer treatment adherence and coordination of support resources
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize cost-related medication underuse as a manifestation of financial toxicity and coordinate assessment, treatment-team communication, and financial/social support to protect adherence and client well-being.

options.A: Recognize possible financial toxicity, assess how treatment costs are affecting adherence and basic needs, and connect the client with the oncology team's financial or social-support resources while notifying the prescribing team about the missed doses.
options.B: Explain that financial toxicity applies only to clients without health insurance, so the main issue is medication noncompliance.
options.C: Tell the client to continue reducing doses independently until finances improve because some treatment is better than none.
options.D: Avoid discussing costs because financial concerns are separate from clinical cancer care and should not influence the nursing plan.

candidate.rationale: NCI defines financial toxicity as problems related to the cost of medical care and notes that it can occur even in people who have health insurance because of copayments, deductibles, coinsurance, treatment-related work loss, and other expenses. Financial toxicity can affect access, quality of life, and treatment adherence; patients may skip doses, take less medication, or not fill prescriptions to save money. The nurse should therefore assess the cost-related barrier, notify the treatment team about missed therapy, and coordinate available financial/social resources rather than labeling the issue as simple noncompliance or endorsing independent dose reduction.
candidate.source_claim_supported: NCI defines financial toxicity as cost-related financial problems that may occur even with health insurance and may reduce access and quality of life. NCI documents behaviors such as skipping doses, taking less medication, or not filling prescriptions because of cost.

candidate.stem: A client receiving oral cancer therapy tells the nurse, 'Even with insurance, the copay is so high that I have been skipping some doses to make the prescription last longer.' Which nursing response is most appropriate?
